subject: Pilot cliffhanger: smoothing proposal and single-license alternative
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearsync.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick ask — pilot extension or usage smoothing?

Hi Tessa,

Hope you’re well. We’re two weeks into our pilot and the model has performed well, but our usage spiked unexpectedly during a data ingestion test last night. The team is concerned we’ll blow through the pilot allocation before we finish the integration checklist.

Options our PM suggested: a short 10–14 day extension, or a one-time usage smoothing credit that covers the spike so we can keep to schedule. We’d prefer not to pay extra up front.

I attached a small CSV with yesterday’s token burn and a note on which flows caused it. Can Redwood offer a short-term concession so we can finish the final set of validations?

If helpful, we can jump on a 20-minute call today.

Thanks,
Ellen
Product Manager, ClearSync
--- Attachment: ClearSync_usage_snapshot.csv (text/csv, 23KB)

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearsync.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@clearsync.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot extension or usage smoothing?

Hi Ellen — thanks for the data, and congrats on the strong results so far.

We can do one of two straightforward paths:
1) 10-day extension at no charge (same terms) — lets you finish the validations without touching your committed runway; or
2) One-time smoothing credit equivalent to ~100k tokens to cover the ingestion spike, applied to the current pilot invoice.

Quick clarifiers from our side: is the spike a one-off test, or likely to repeat during the remaining pilot? If it’s repeatable, the extension plus a reduced credit might be safer.

I’m available at 11:30 PT if you want to chat. If you prefer, we can put a formal addendum in DocuSign today.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192
--- Attachment: none

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: FW: ClearSync pilot spike — ask: extension vs smoothing credit

Looping you both in — ClearSync hit a vape-like spike during ingestion tests. Ellen asked for either a 10–14 day extension or a one-time smoothing credit (approx 100k tokens).

I want to balance: keep the account moving, avoid setting a precedent for big credits, and limit legal churn. My proposed approach: offer a free 10-day extension + a 25% smoothing credit (25k tokens) as a one-time courtesy if they sign the addendum today. If finance signs off, we can add an SLA note that repeated operational spikes will move them to a short-term burst surcharge.

Can you confirm if 25k token credit (~$225 at current rate) is within our AE approval band? If not, I’ll request a formal concession from pricing. Also flag any legal language we should include in the addendum.

Thanks — Tessa

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: ClearSync pilot spike — ask: extension vs smoothing credit

Tessa — 25k token credit is fine from a finance perspective (small hit versus risk of losing momentum). Please include: 1) extension window dates, 2) one-time credit amount and expiration, 3) a sentence clarifying that credits are non-recurring and apply only to pilot account, and 4) optional clause for surge protection pricing if usage patterns change.

Kimberly — from legal side, keep the addendum lightweight: attach it as a one-page pilot addendum; do not change core SLA language. If they ask for broader term edits, send to legal intake.

I’ll approve the DocuSign envelope if you want to send the draft.

-rishi
Head of Sales Operations
--- Attachment: none

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearsync.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@clearsync.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Formal proposal: 10-day extension + one-time smoothing credit (pilot addendum)

Hi Ellen and Marco — thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Per our conversation, here’s the formal, time-limited proposal to keep your validation on track: 

What we’re offering
- A 10-day extension of the current pilot (new end date: 2026-11-20) at no additional charge.
- A one-time smoothing credit of 25,000 tokens applied to your current pilot allocation. Credit will be consumed first and expires at the pilot end date.

Terms and guardrails
- Credits are a one-time courtesy for this pilot only; they do not change future billing or committed packages.
- If ClearSync’s ingestion tests indicate sustained higher usage, we’ll work with you to scope a burst buffer or discuss a short-term surge plan (pricing in the addendum).
- Addendum is one page, no SLA changes.

Next steps
- If this works, sign the attached addendum (DocuSign link below) by 2026-11-05 and we’ll apply the extension immediately.
- If you need a larger smoothing amount instead of extension, let me know and I’ll escalate to pricing for a one-time review.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/projects/CLRS-ADD-002
Attachment: Redwood_Pilot_Addendum_v2.pdf (pilot addendum draft)

Happy to jump on a final 10-minute call to walk through.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: Redwood_Pilot_Addendum_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 45KB)

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearsync.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@clearsync.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Formal proposal: 10-day extension + one-time smoothing credit (pilot addendum)

Tessa — that looks perfect. We’ll sign the addendum today (targeting noon PT) and confirm once DocuSign completes. Appreciate the quick turn.

One quick operational ask: once signed, can Redwood temporarily raise the per-minute API retry window for our ingestion flow? That would reduce the immediate load while we patch. If so, please point to the ops contact and timeline.

Thanks again — Ellen
Product Manager, ClearSync
